description: Equipo de Universidad Autónoma de Campeche
summary:
Kanan Ka'ax ("guardian of the forest" in Maya) is a web application that helps communities in the Yucatán Peninsula plan agricultural burns safely and anticipate wildfire risk. It combines NASA Earth observation data on active fires, weather, and vegetation into an interactive burn calendar that shows when and where conditions are safe or dangerous for burning.

At its core is NAL, our fire prediction model, which forecasts fire activity for a specific year or a range of years, so farmers, local authorities, and civil protection teams can prepare in advance instead of reacting once a fire has started.

Uncontrolled agricultural burns are one of the leading causes of wildfires in the region, destroying forest, harming air quality, and threatening livelihoods. Kanan Ka'ax turns open satellite data into clear, local, actionable guidance that protects both traditional farming practices and the forest they depend on.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Kanan Ka'ax ("to care for the forest" in Yucatec Maya) is a burn calendar from space. Satellites have recorded fire hot spots for 25 years, but the record is split between MODIS, which is reaching the end of its life, and VIIRS, which sees 3 to 6 times more detections for the same fires. Joined as they are, the two records give false trends: uncorrected, 2024 looks like the worst fire year in Yucatán; harmonized, it is the 3rd of 25.

HOW IT WORKS

1. We read NASA FIRMS hot spots from MODIS and VIIRS (NOAA-20) and count them on a 0.25° grid, month by month.

2. We harmonize both sensors into one VIIRS-equivalent record, November 2000 to November 2026. Five methods were compared on held-out years and the best one was kept: the median monthly error drops from 73.2% to 10.0% (R² 0.986).

3. A web app turns the record into plain answers. You type your town or click the map and get three answers: when it burns the most, how this year is going, and whether anything unusual happened. It also shows a year-by-month burning calendar, alerts, a weekly risk map built with NASA POWER climate, protected areas and the official burning season.

4. NAL, our forecast engine, shows the areas and months of highest risk for the years you choose (2027 to 2031), always with a range. Tested on 15 years it had never seen, the 3 months it expected the most fire in held 85% of the real fire (the best possible was 86%).

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Fire brigades, Civil Protection, protected-area managers and farming communities can finally compare this season with history and get ahead of the critical months. Alerts can be checked: the tool flagged unusual fire next to the Yum Balam reserve in June 2024, and we verified it with before-and-after NASA HLS imagery and NASA OPERA (82.5% of the hot spots fall on mapped vegetation loss, against 11.3% of random points). In 2026, one in five fires in Yucatán state burned outside the legal burning season (20.2%, the highest in 26 years).

TOOLS

Python for the data pipeline, the validation and the training of NAL. HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Leaflet for the web app, which is a static page hosted on GitHub Pages (no server needed). Data: NASA FIRMS, NASA POWER and NASA GIBS (Blue Marble, HLS, OPERA DIST-ALERT); partner data from NOAA (El Niño index), WDPA protected areas, OpenStreetMap and Copernicus Sentinel-2 through HLS. Git and GitHub for version control. An AI tool (Claude, by Anthropic) assisted with code and documentation; the team reviewed and ran everything and is responsible for the results.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

It asks questions other fire maps do not: does fire follow the legal burning calendar? Is it a farm burn or a wildfire (51% of detections come from small one-day burns, 14% from large or long fires)? What is coming next year? The calendar can also be listened to, one note per month, and every answer is written in words a grandparent can understand, in English and Spanish.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Honesty first: every number comes from held-out tests, ranges are shown instead of single values, and results that did not work are reported too. Accessibility: a colour ramp that works for colour-blind users and never colour alone. Privacy: your location never leaves your browser. Low cost: a static page that runs on any phone or laptop. Reach: the same code, unchanged, runs in Portugal and recovers its worst known fire years (2005, 2003, 2017); a new region needs only a configuration file.
